Subject: POC: Capacity planning & success criteria - Acme AI

Hi Priya / James —

Thanks again for the discovery call today. Quick recap + proposed next steps so we can lock the POC plan and hardware footprint.

Recap / success criteria (proposed)
- Goal: validate inference latency and cost for your multimodal recommendation model under production-like traffic.
- Success criteria: 95th pct latency <= 420ms for 1024-token text+image requests, and cost per 1M tokens <= $X (we'll provide an estimate).
- Secondary: validate autoscaling behavior with cold-starts < 30s for new workers and no error rate > 0.5%.

POC scope & timeline
- Duration: 2 weeks of active testing + 1 week buffer for tweaks (proposed start: Mon Mar 22).
- Deliverables: capacity plan, test harness (load scripts), dashboards (latency / cost / traces), final recommendations.

Initial capacity ask (proposal)
- Reserved baseline: 2 x A100-80GB equivalent GPUs (reserved for the two-week POC).
- Autoscaling policy: allow burst to 4 GPUs for short spikes (up to 10 minutes) with automated cooldown.
- Pre-warm option: we can pre-warm 1 additional worker before high-traffic windows to reduce cold-starts.

What we need from Acme AI
- Representative test dataset + sample requests and a short list of high-priority workflows.
- Desired concurrency/throughput targets (RPS or concurrent requests) for our load plan.
- Confirmation on any restricted regions or compliance constraints.

Attachments: redwood_poc_capacity_plan.xlsx (detailed numbers + cost estimate) and infra-cost-estimate.pdf.

Next steps / owners
- Priya: confirm success criteria + provide sample payloads by Fri Mar 12.
- James: reply with expected peak concurrency and any model size constraints.
- Dev (SE): finalize autoscale thresholds and pre-warm approach.
- Me (Marissa): coordinate SOW and schedule kickoff once capacity is agreed.

If that looks good I can send a SOW and proposed reserved capacity purchase for signing.

Thanks,
Marissa Cole

Thanks Marissa — this is really helpful. A few clarifications from our side:

1) Latency goal: the 95th <= 420ms is aggressive but reasonable; can we confirm if that target assumes batching of requests or single-request latency? We generally send small batches for recommendations (~4 items).
2) Concurrency: for the POC we expect mid-day peaks of ~180 concurrent sessions, with avg sustained ~60 RPS. Will the baseline 2 GPUs handle sustained 60 RPS?
3) Cost: can you call out the expected incremental cost for the reserved baseline vs burst? We need a quick number to justify budget to procurement.
4) Compliance: we need the SOC2 questionnaire answered (we've started the form) and the SOW to include data retention terms.

We'll aim to get test payloads and a small sample model artifact to you by Mon Mar 15.

Thanks — Priya

Hi all — quick technical notes to address Priya's questions: 

- Latency: the proposed 95th ms assumes single-request (no intentional batching) for a 1024-token multimodal request on our optimized runtime. If you plan to batch client-side (n=4) we can update the numbers to show improved throughput/latency.

- Throughput per GPU: on a model similar to your size, one A100-80GB should sustain ~50-80 concurrent small requests depending on prompt size and KV cache hit rate. So 2 reserved GPUs as baseline + autoscale to 4 for spikes aligns with your ~180 concurrent peak if bursts are short and we hit KV cache benefits.

- Autoscaling behavior: we propose health-check-based scale-up when 95th latency crosses 350ms for >45s OR CPU/GPU utilization > 70% for >60s. Scale one replica at a time with a cooldown of 10 minutes. For predictable bursts we recommend scheduled pre-warm for known windows.

- Pre-warm and warm pools: we can keep a pre-warmed spare worker (no model load time) which effectively reduces cold-start latency to ~5s for routing. Full cold-start with model load can be ~30-60s depending on quantization.

- Cost notes: reserved baseline pricing is lower per-hour than burst capacity; I'll attach a rough infra-cost-estimate.pdf with hourly numbers. Exact numbers depend on region and instance family.

I'll update the attached spreadsheet with these thresholds. Happy to jump on a quick tech sync if helpful.

Thanks,
Dev Patel
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
dev@redwood.com

- For bursts up to 180 concurrent, you mentioned KV cache. If we don't have a warm KV cache initially (fresh model + new dataset), how much of an impact do you expect on peak latency?
- Also curious about fallback model variants — if a 70B runs too slowly under load, can we test a quantized 14B variant as a fallback during the POC?

Would be great to include both scenarios in the POC plan so we can show execs the tradeoffs.

Hi Priya / James —

Thanks for the quick turn responses — circling back with a consolidated plan and owners so we can kick off on Mon Mar 22 as discussed.

Finalized POC plan (agreed items)
- Success criteria: 95th pct latency <= 420ms single-request; show cost baseline for reserved 2x A100-80GB and delta for burst to 4 GPUs.
- Baseline capacity: 2 x A100-80GB reserved for the POC window.
- Autoscale: scale when 95th > 350ms for >45s or GPU util > 70% for >60s; scale one replica at a time; cooldown 10 minutes.
- Burst: allow up to 4 GPUs for up to 10 minutes per burst; scheduled pre-warm available for known traffic windows.
- Fallback model variant: include a quantized 14B variant test path in the load plan (Dev will run side-by-side comparison and record latencies/costs).

Owners & dates
- Marissa (AE): finalize SOW and reserved capacity agreement by Thu Mar 19. DocuSign link: https://www.docusign.com/sign/XYZ-ACME-POC-SOW
- Priya (PM, Acme): deliver sample payloads and expected concurrency by Mon Mar 15 (you flagged Mar 15 in your note).
- James (Eng, Acme): share a small sample model artifact or spec for the 70B variant by Mon Mar 15.
- Dev (SE): finalize autoscale thresholds and prepare load harness + run the first load tests during week of Mar 22.

Attachments included: redwood_poc_capacity_plan.xlsx, infra-cost-estimate.pdf, sow-template.docx.

If you confirm, I'll place the reserved capacity order and schedule a 60-min kickoff for Mon Mar 22 at 10:00am PT with tech leads.
